pairs.why: Real clock is a straight-on face against a flat striped wall with no ground; A keeps that, while B adds a floor line and cast shadow that make it stand in a room.
Both put a front-facing jellyfish in the middle of a radial burst with the same shallow depth, and neither has the real card's diagonal pose and soft depth gradient.
B has a bigger hero, a closer camera and fewer depth layers, like the real close-up; A is a far wide shot with a small dock and a long horizon.
A uses the real cards' 3/4 front view at a moderate camera height with the hero on a simple ground, while B shows more top face with a flatter, more boxy view.
A has the closer, higher camera that shows the table top and a tilted ground, with a large hero and foreground grass like the real card; B is lower and farther with a flatter, more distant horizon.
Both are nearly frontal, but B has slightly more of the real card's tilted top plane and visible side thickness.
A's hero is larger and viewed from a slightly higher angle so the roof top reads, as in the real card; B is smaller, with less of the roof visible.
A has the real card's high camera looking down on the water and posts, with the hero filling the frame and little sky; B is a lower, farther view with a big sky and a visible horizon.
